# Shutdown and Trade Risk

**Summary.** Our season ends on 2027-03-28, so March rest hurts us in the weeks that decide the title. Shutdown risk sits mostly with teams that have no reason to win or lose in March, such as Brooklyn, Milwaukee, the Clippers, New Orleans and Dallas, plus teams that may rest veterans. Pay the low end of a player's range when his March minutes are uncertain, sell those players before the 2027-03-04 deadline, and save FAB for young players whose roles grow after veterans are traded.

## Which teams create March risk

Once a team decides to tank, it may shut down injured players for the rest of the season, even players who could have returned. In our league that loss lands in weeks 19 to 21, when every game counts. ([08-17](https://youtu.be/LcZcvk8s1xQ?t=890))

Teams that do not control their own pick are a separate risk. The notes name the Nets, Bucks, Clippers, Pelicans and Mavericks. They have no reason to tank and no reason to push for wins. So they may rest players, be extra careful with injuries, or give young players minutes late in the season. Brooklyn and Milwaukee are the main examples. ([08-21](https://youtu.be/uRsfijpBPok?t=1851), [07-13](https://youtu.be/Rqb5GdrSweY?t=1333), [07-14](https://youtu.be/xHRF06_E9HE?t=127))

A team with nothing to play for in March can cut its veterans' minutes to develop young players. The same goes for stars on bad teams. Value them on a range that includes rest and fewer minutes, not just on per-game value. In practice, bid near the bottom of their fair price range, not the top. ([09-26](https://youtu.be/3UGI05PDvrE?t=220), [09-30](https://youtu.be/MUbNYdjpUDM?t=372))

## Shutdown risk in weeks 19 to 21

Julius Randle matters most here. Brooklyn may rest him in March so young players get time, and that cuts straight into our playoff weeks. Draft him only inside his fair range, and plan to trade him before the 2027-03-04 deadline. After that date you cannot move him in our league. ([Julius Randle](../profiles/players/julius-randle.md), [09-26](https://youtu.be/3UGI05PDvrE?t=220), [07-13](https://youtu.be/Rqb5GdrSweY?t=1333))

Michael Porter Jr. and Moritz Wagner are also on Brooklyn, and their March minutes are uncertain. Porter is still worth drafting, but keep your bid in the lower part of his range. Wagner is a waiver name only. ([Michael Porter Jr.](../profiles/players/michael-porter.md), [Moritz Wagner](../profiles/players/moritz-wagner.md), [08-21](https://youtu.be/uRsfijpBPok?t=1851))

Darius Garland carries only a small risk of late-season rest on the Clippers. That small risk does not change his fair price, but check his minutes in February before you decide whether to hold him for the playoffs. Golden State may rest Draymond Green and Al Horford for lottery odds. Both are fringe players, so the risk only matters if you pick them up. Sacramento could pull Zach LaVine's minutes or bench him as it builds for the future. ([Darius Garland](../profiles/players/darius-garland.md), [Draymond Green](../profiles/players/draymond-green.md), [Al Horford](../profiles/players/al-horford.md), [Zach LaVine](../profiles/players/zach-lavine.md))

Dallas is a no-pick team with a playoff schedule of 4, 4 and 4 games. Kyrie Irving could get only 10 of those games if he keeps resting on back-to-backs. Milwaukee is a no-pick team too, so watch the minutes of Ryan Rollins and Tyler Herro in February. ([Kyrie Irving](../profiles/players/kyrie-irving.md), [08-21](https://youtu.be/uRsfijpBPok?t=1851), [Ryan Rollins](../profiles/players/ryan-rollins.md), [Tyler Herro](../profiles/players/tyler-herro.md))

## Trade risk: when a move cuts value

Projections assume trade candidates stay all season, so they do not price in a role change. For some players a trade is the main downside. A trade to a good team could cut Domantas Sabonis's role. A deal could lower Porter's usage further and shrink Cameron Johnson's role. A move into a third-option role would sink Norman Powell's value. Do not pay extra for these players because of trade hopes. ([09-03](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=1397), [Domantas Sabonis](../profiles/players/domantas-sabonis.md), [Michael Porter Jr.](../profiles/players/michael-porter.md), [Cameron Johnson](../profiles/players/cameron-johnson.md), [Norman Powell](../profiles/players/norman-powell.md))

Several early-round guards also carry trade tags: Jamal Murray (salary), Austin Reaves (if the Lakers struggle) and Trey Murphy III (high asking price). The notes do not say a trade would hurt their stats. So pay their normal prices, and check trade news each week from January until 2027-03-04. ([Jamal Murray](../profiles/players/jamal-murray.md), [Austin Reaves](../profiles/players/austin-reaves.md), [Trey Murphy III](../profiles/players/trey-murphy.md))

Rudy Gobert could be traded if Minnesota's season goes badly. Minnesota also plays only two games in our week 20, so a punt FT team should plan a streaming spot for that week. Mark Williams is expected back only in mid to late March and may be traded at the deadline. At best he is a short playoff pickup. ([Rudy Gobert](../profiles/players/rudy-gobert.md), [Mark Williams](../profiles/players/mark-williams.md))

## Where the experts disagree

The experts split on two veterans. On Kyrie Irving, several experts say a trade is possible, but one heard no trade talk. On Jrue Holiday, one expert said in June that he will likely be moved, but a later team preview doubts a consolidation trade. Anthony Davis is expected to stay in Washington, but the Golden State rumors leave a deadline move possible. For all three, draft on current role and price, and do not pay for a trade that may not come. ([Kyrie Irving](../profiles/players/kyrie-irving.md), [Jrue Holiday](../profiles/players/jrue-holiday.md), [Anthony Davis](../profiles/players/anthony-davis.md))

## Young players who could gain

Because projections assume veterans stay, they can understate the young players behind them. The clearest case is Orlando. It is near the second apron and likely has to choose between Jalen Suggs and Anthony Black. A Suggs trade or injury is what would make Black startable. ([09-03](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=1397), [Anthony Black](../profiles/players/anthony-black.md), [Jalen Suggs](../profiles/players/jalen-suggs.md))

Other waiver names to track: Scoot Henderson is named as a likely outgoing piece in a rumored Jaylen Brown trade. Malik Monk could be traded into a bigger role. Burries is Milwaukee's long-term shooting guard behind Herro. Kasparas Jakučionis needs real minutes in that crowded backcourt or a trade. In Chicago, Jalen Smith's role is tied to Leonard Miller. Add Smith at once if he starts. ([Scoot Henderson](../profiles/players/scoot-henderson.md), [Malik Monk](../profiles/players/malik-monk.md), [Tyler Herro](../profiles/players/tyler-herro.md), [Kasparas Jakučionis](../profiles/players/kasparas-jakucionis.md), [Jalen Smith](../profiles/players/jalen-smith.md))

Plan for it. Keep part of your FAB for the days around 2027-03-04, and keep one roster spot open for a moved or promoted player. We get only 6 acquisitions per week. In weeks 19 to 21, spend them on players who are sure to play. ([09-03](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=1397), [09-26](https://youtu.be/3UGI05PDvrE?t=220))
